pull.title: build: Bump macOS SDK version to 15.0
pull.body:
Qt 6.12, which supports deployment targets up to macOS 26, requires the macOS 15 SDK or higher.

See https://doc.qt.io/qt-6.12/macos.html.

This is a prerequisite for the upcoming update of Qt in depends from 6.8 LTS to 6.12 LTS.

> requires the macOS 15 SDK or higher.

What is the actual requirement for the `15.x` SDK?

> > requires the macOS 15 SDK or higher.
> 
> What is the actual requirement for the `15.x` SDK?

It's hard to say from the [commit](https://github.com/qt/qtbase/commit/21d71d1a991a2009e93ed7302b3ec3ce21d3c87f) message. But the configuration fails with the current `OSX_SDK_VERSION=14.0`.

comments.body:
> See https://doc.qt.io/qt-6.12/macos.html.

This page also claims that a deployment target of 14.4 or later is required, but you're not changing that here. Will our release binaries just crash on the older versions?

> This page also claims that a deployment target of 14.4 or later is required, but you're not changing that here.

Yes, both changes are prerequisites for updating Qt to 6.12. However, I thought it would be better to consider them separately, as we might skip no longer supported 14.4 altogether and bump the minimum version straight to 15.0.

> Yes, both changes are prerequisites for updating Qt to 6.12.

I don't see the other change in #36593?

Can you explain what this value means for non-Apple people? According to https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode-release-notes/xcode-26_1-release-notes?changes=l_4,l_4,l_4,l_4&utm_source=openai#Overview, Xcode 26.1.1 includes [...] SDKs for [...] 26.1, so this value should be 26.1 and neither 14 nor 15?



<details><summary>I think this is also what Ralph LLM asks:</summary>

The pinned sysroot comes from Xcode 26.1.1/17B100 and contains the macOS 26.1 SDK, but the linker receives 15.0 as the SDK version and the Guix symbol checker requires that value. Builds using this sysroot therefore report SDK 15.0 in their Mach-O metadata despite using the macOS 26.1 SDK. Could the linker metadata and checker use the actual SDK version while keeping OSX_MIN_VERSION=14.0? If Qt needs a separate SDK floor, keep that separate rather than using one value for both. ([developer.apple.com](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode-release-notes/xcode-26_1-release-notes?changes=l_4%2Cl_4%2Cl_4%2Cl_4&utm_source=openai))

</details>


Basically, I wonder why is this not 26.1 now. Going further, this line could also be removed on the next archive bump and the actual version could simply be extracted from `SDKSettings.json`'s version field?

> Can you explain what this value means for non-Apple people? The linker stamps the SDK version into the binary. At runtime, Apple’s frameworks read it to decide which generation of behaviour the binary opts into, independently of the headers actually used and of the minimum supported macOS version. Choosing 26.1 means the binary opts into every behaviour change Apple has gated up to macOS 26.1, so on any OS that has them, the latest ones are used. Choosing 15.0 means the binary opts into changes gated up to macOS 15.0 and keeps the legacy behaviour for anything gated later. This choice affects the look-and-feel of the GUI. Consider the following side-by-side comparison of `OSX_SDK_VERSION=14.0` and `OSX_SDK_VERSION=26.1` on macOS 27.2:

Thanks for clarifying!

Though, I still wonder why this is not 26.1 now (i.e. the latest SDK), so that any OS can use the latest features, if it has them. Is there some requirement that GUI looks the same for any macOS version? Or is this some hack in the assumption that gating the features will avoid having an exploding test matrix?

Personally, I think it is fine to  let the GUI look different (possibly "modern" on later macOS versions). Also I think it is fine to use other SDK features on later macOS versions. If there was a bug in any of them, we'd have to fix them anyway for self-compilation and if there is a macOS bug a feature gate is no guarantee that the bug won't happen?

Just curious. Any value here seems fine, given your reply.

> Though, I still wonder why this is not 26.1 now (i.e. the latest SDK), so that any OS can use the latest features, if it has them.

That would require us to test the release binaries on every supported macOS version, with each one running a different generation of framework behaviour.

> Is there some requirement that GUI looks the same for any macOS version?

No, there is not, as far as I'm aware.

> Or is this some hack in the assumption that gating the features will avoid having an exploding test matrix?

Yes, that is my thinking.

> Personally, I think it is fine to let the GUI look different (possibly "modern" on later macOS versions). Also I think it is fine to use other SDK features on later macOS versions. If there was a bug in any of them, we'd have to fix them anyway for self-compilation and if there is a macOS bug a feature gate is no guarantee that the bug won't happen?

To use the latest SDK, it's needed to build with Homebrew’s packages.
